text:
alex: Heads-up — CI is failing on the eval-runner for the new quantized Llama-2 variant. I think it’s a batchkey collision when synthetic prompts get deduped. Logs below.

alex: ```
ERROR Runner: duplicate batch key for shard=3 key=anchor:1234
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "runner/queue.py", line 412, in enqueue_batch
    assert key not in active_batches
AssertionError
```

tara: @alex ah, same job that flaked yesterday?

miguel: Not the same. Pattern looks different — the batching key is `prompt_fingerprint + shard_id`. Our synthetic generator sometimes reuses anchor ids when `--reuse-seed` is on.

jin: I can repro locally with a tiny loop.

jin: ```bash
python tests/repro_batchkey.py --seed 42 --count 500
# reproduces duplicate anchor:1234 in ~2 seconds
```

alex: CI job: eval/runner/sync-quantize failed — http://ci.internal/jobs/3221 (logs attached in job) :eyes:

tara: Short-term: we should gate the CI to skip the synthetic-heavy shard so we don't block rollouts. Long-term: include prompt_instance_id in the batch key.

miguel: Agreed. Also add a debug assert that logs the full prompt payload when duplicates happen so we can tell whether it’s true dedupe or a generator bug.

jin: I'll open a small PR to append `instance_idx` to the batch key and add a unit test that runs `repro_batchkey.py` as part of the runner test.

jin: PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runner/pull/412 — adds `+ ':' + str(instance_idx)` to `make_batch_key()` and a test.

alex: @miguel can you watch the canary after the PR? If it looks stable we can remove the temporary CI skip.

miguel: Yep, will monitor. I'll also add the debug assertion as a follow-up.

eval-ci-bot: Job rerun #3221.1 — succeeded (runtime 3m12s)

alex: Awesome — leaving this thread for postmortem notes. Follow-ups: add generator guard to avoid anchor reuse, land the batchkey change, add a metric on duplicate-batchkey rate. :thumbsup:
